in_hebrew.name: מתיאוש
in_hebrew.meaning: מתנה אלוהים, שוער אלוהים, אחד הנביאים
in_hebrew.long_meaning: מתיאוש הוא שם עברי שמשמעותו 'מתנה אלוהים' או 'שוער אלוהים'. השם מתוארך לתקופת המקרא וקשור לנביא מתיאוש, ששימש כשליח אלוהים להפיץ את דברו בקרב בני האדם. השם מעיד על חשיבות הנבואה והשליחות בתרבות היהודית והנוצרית.

in_greek.name: Ματθαῖος
in_greek.meaning: δώρο του Θεού, απόστολος του Θεού
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Ματθαῖος είναι όνομα ελληνικό που σημαίνει 'δώρο του Θεού' ή 'απόστολος του Θεού'. Το όνομα αυτό συσχετίζεται με τον Ματθαῖο, έναν από τους δώδεκα αποστόλους του Ιησού Χριστού, που ήταν σημαντικός στην πρώιμη Εκκλησία. Το όνομα αντανακλά τη σημασία της αποστολής και του ευαγγελισμού στην παράδοση των πρώτων Χριστιανών.

in_latin.name: Mateusz
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Mateusz significat 'donum Dei' vel 'apostolus Dei'. Hoc nomen in traditione christiana primitiva invenitur et refertur ad Mattathiam, apostolum Iesu Christi. Nomen hoc importat significationem muneris et apostolatus in Ecclesia primitiva.

in_english.name: Mateusz
in_english.meaning: Gift of God, Godly gift, or Apostle
in_english.long_meaning: The name Mateusz is derived from the Hebrew name 'Mattityahu' (מתתיהו), meaning 'gift of God' or 'God's gift'. It is associated with Matthew, one of Jesus Christ's twelve apostles and the author of the Gospel of Matthew. The name signifies a divine gift and reflects the importance of apostleship and evangelism in Christian tradition. Historically, the name has been popularized in various cultures, particularly in Eastern European countries.

biblical_reference.note: The name Mateusz is directly related to Matthew, a tax collector and one of Jesus' twelve apostles.

data.cultural_impact: The name Mateusz has been popular in various Eastern European countries, particularly in Poland. It's often used as a masculine given name, not just among Christians but also among other religious groups. The name is also used in other Slavic nations, albeit less frequently.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Mateusz evokes a strong spiritual association with the Christian faith, as it is derived from Matthias, one of the twelve apostles who replaced Judas Iscariot. Matthias was chosen as an apostle based on the criteria of having been "numbered among us from the beginning" (Acts 1:13) and "witnesses from the beginning" (Acts 1:21-22) - implying steadfastness, faith, and commitment to the teachings of Jesus. In the Catholic Church, Mateusz is the patron saint of various causes, including select professions, towns, and regions. Above all, the name encourages its bearer to embody the virtues of loyalty, trustworthiness, and faith, reflecting the spiritual journey of the apostle who was chosen by God himself.

It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.
